{{eastern name  order|Pyber László}}
'''''László Pyber''''' (born 8 May 1960 in [[Budapest]]) is a [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]]. He is a researcher at the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]], Budapest. He works in [[combinatorics]] and [[group theory]].

== Biography ==
Pyber received his Ph.D. from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] in 1989 under the direction of [[László Lovász]] and [[Gyula O. H. Katona|Gyula O.H. Katona]] with the thesis ''Extremal Structures and Covering Problems.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=132736|title=László Pyber – The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

In 2007, he was awarded the Academics Prize by the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mta.hu/dijak-kituntetesek/akademiai-dij-105787|title=Akadémiai Díj|date=February 2016 }}</ref>

In 2017, he was the recipient of an [[European Research Council|ERC]] Advanced Grant.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/rcn/210050/factsheet/en|title=Growth in Groups and Graph Isomorphism Now}}</ref>

== Mathematical contributions ==
Pyber has solved a number of [[conjecture]]s in [[graph theory]]. In 1985, he proved the conjecture of [[Paul Erdős]] and [[Tibor Gallai]] that edges of a [[simple graph]] with ''n'' vertices can be covered with at most ''n''−1 circuits and edges.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber|first=László|title=An Erdös-Gallai conjecture|journal=Combinatorica|volume=5|pages=67–79|doi=10.1007/BF02579444|year=1985|s2cid=30972963 }}</ref> In 1986, he proved the conjecture of [[Paul Erdős]] that a graph with ''n'' vertices and its complement can be covered with ''n''<sup>2</sup>/4 + 2 [[clique (graph theory)|clique]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber|first=László|title=Clique convering of graphs|journal=Combinatorica|volume=6|issue=4|pages=393–398|doi=10.1007/BF02579265|year=1986|s2cid=40109732 }}</ref>

He has also contributed to the study of [[permutation group]]s. In 1993, he provided an upper bound for the [[order (group theory)|order]] of a 2-transitive group of degree ''n'' not containing ''[[Alternating group|A<sub>n</sub>]]'' avoiding the use of the [[classification of finite simple groups]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber|first=László|title=On the orders of doubly transitive permutation groups, elementary estimates|journal=Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A|volume=62|issue=2|pages=361–366|doi=10.1016/0097-3165(93)90053-B|year=1993|doi-access=free}}</ref> Together with [[Tomasz Łuczak]], Pyber proved the conjecture of [[John McKay (mathematician)|McKay]] that for every ''ε''>0, there is a constant ''C'' such that ''C'' randomly chosen elements invariably generate the [[symmetric group]] ''S''<sub>''n''</sub> with probability greater than 1−''ε''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber and Łuczak|title=On Random Generation of the Symmetric Group|journal=Combinatorics, Probability and Computing|volume=2|issue=4|pages=505–512|doi=10.1017/S0963548300000869|year=1993|s2cid=34255045 }}</ref>

Pyber has made fundamental contributions in enumerating [[finite group]]s of a given order ''n''. In 1993, he proved<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber|first=László|title=Enumerating finite groups of given order|url=https://annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/13662|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=137|pages=203–220|doi=10.2307/2946623|jstor=2946623|year=1993|issue=1 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> that if the [[prime decomposition]] of ''n'' is ''n''=''p''<sub>1</sub><sup>''g''<sub>1</sub></sup>  ⋯ ''p''<sub>''k''</sub><sup>''g''<sub>''k''</sub></sup> and ''&mu;=''max(''g''<sub>1</sub>,...,''g''<sub>k</sub>), then the number of groups of order ''n'' is at most{{center|<math>n^{(\frac{2}{27}+o(1))\mu^2}.</math>}}In 2004, Pyber settled several questions in [[subgroup growth]] by completing the investigation of the spectrum of possible subgroup growth types.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber|first=László|title=Groups of intermediate subgroup growth and a problem of Grothendieck|journal=Duke Mathematical Journal|volume=121|pages=169–188|doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-04-12115-3|year=2004}}</ref>

<!--* Felállította azt a sejtést, hogy majdnem minden véges csoport nilpotens. Ha ez igaz, akkor a legtöbb véges csoport 2-csoport.-->

In 2011, Pyber and Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain obtained a surprisingly explicit formula for the number of random elements needed to generate a finite ''d''-generator group with high probability.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jaikin-Zapirain and Pyber|title=Random generation of finite and profinite groups and group enumeration|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=173|issue=2|pages=769–814|doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.2.4|year=2011|doi-access=free|hdl=10486/662154|hdl-access=free}}</ref> They also explored related questions for [[profinite group]]s and settled several [[open problem]]s.

In 2016, Pyber and Endre Szabó proved that in a [[list of finite simple groups|finite simple group]] ''L'' of Lie type, a generating set ''A'' of ''L'' either grows, i.e., |''A''<sup>3</sup>| ≥ |''A''|<sup>1+''ε''</sup> for some ''ε'' depending only on the Lie rank of ''L'', or ''A''<sup>3</sup>=''L''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Pyber and Szabo|title=Growth in finite simple groups of Lie type|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=29|pages=95–146|doi=10.1090/S0894-0347-2014-00821-3|year=2014|arxiv=1001.4556|s2cid=51800011 }}</ref> This implies that diameters of [[Cayley graph]]s of finite simple groups of bounded rank are polylogarithmic in the size of the group, partially resolving a well-known conjecture of [[László Babai]].
